data.name: Ethereal Legends
data.detailed_description:
Ethereal Legends is a modern indie action RPG, built (mostly) by one person in Unreal Engine 4 for PC, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.

A powerful foe has descended upon the world of Arcadia. The Ethereal Knights, protectors of the realm, have nearly all been destroyed.

Only you remain.

Enter the portal and defend the Ethereal Realms from the evil which plagues them. Battle deadly monsters and huge bosses, wield numerous weapons, cast powerful spells, solve challenging puzzles, and use all the tools at your disposal to put an end to the madness.

Active Combat

Your combat style is determined by the spells, weapons, and armor you choose to equip. With 3 distinct weapon types and a great number of spells, items, and armor pieces to choose from, you are provided with countless options to defeat your enemies.

Environment Puzzles

A plethora of brain teasers awaits deep within the darkest corners of Arcadia. Explore and interact with the world around you to unlock new paths and discover secrets hidden in the Ethereal Realms.

Epic High Fantasy

A pure story of good versus evil. Explore gorgeous elemental locales reaching into the sky and beyond. Battle massive enemies, experience the powerful soundtrack, and enjoy a beautifully rendered fantasy world powered by Unreal Engine 4.

Open Source

Want to build your own game, based on Ethereal Legends? You can! The C++ code used to create this game can be found on Github, under the open source Apache 2.0 license. Maybe you simply want to help make Ethereal better. This is the place to start! I welcome all contributions, and successful pull requests will have their author credited in-game.

Nvidia Ansel Support

Nvidia Ansel is an amazing photography feature built into to Ethereal Legends. Ansel allows players with Nvidia GeForce GTX 650 or better graphics cards to take beautiful high resolution or 360 degree screenshots while in game.

reviews.review:
Ethereal Legends is an independent fantasy action RPG that combines third-person combat, magical abilities, exploration, and environmental puzzles into an ambitious adventure. Developed and published by Soverance Studios, the game follows the last surviving Ethereal Knight, a warrior determined to save the realm of Arcadia from an ancient evil. Its traditional fantasy setting features mysterious portals, supernatural landscapes, dangerous creatures, and formidable enemies. Although its presentation lacks the refinement of larger productions, the game demonstrates considerable creative ambition and offers an interesting experience for players who appreciate lesser-known fantasy adventures.

The storyline revolves around a familiar conflict between good and evil, with the destruction of the Ethereal Knights establishing the protagonist's motivation. This straightforward premise provides a clear objective and allows players to concentrate on exploration and combat. However, the narrative rarely develops beyond its conventional foundations. Character development is limited, and the world could benefit from more substantial lore, memorable interactions, and unexpected developments. While the simplicity makes the adventure accessible, players expecting sophisticated storytelling or meaningful narrative choices may find the experience underwhelming.

Combat is the central gameplay feature, incorporating melee weapons, magical attacks, and equipment customization. Three weapon categories provide different offensive possibilities, while spells, armor, and consumable items introduce additional tactical options. These mechanics encourage experimentation and allow players to approach encounters with varying strategies. Unfortunately, the combat system does not consistently achieve the responsiveness and precision expected from polished action RPGs. Movement, attack animations, and enemy behavior can feel somewhat unrefined, reducing the satisfaction of otherwise promising encounters. Nevertheless, the combination of physical and magical abilities provides enough variety to make battles occasionally entertaining.

Boss encounters represent some of the game's more ambitious moments. Powerful enemies challenge players to manage positioning, recognize attack opportunities, and make effective use of their equipment. These confrontations contribute to the sense of danger and provide important milestones throughout the adventure. However, inconsistent combat feedback and limited mechanical sophistication can diminish their impact. Players familiar with demanding action RPGs may notice shortcomings in encounter design, particularly when enemy behavior becomes predictable. Despite these weaknesses, the larger battles help reinforce the game's heroic fantasy atmosphere.

Exploration provides a welcome alternative to constant fighting. Players travel through mysterious environments, investigate hidden pathways, and solve puzzles to progress through different locations. Environmental challenges encourage observation and add variety to the gameplay, preventing the adventure from becoming entirely combat-focused. The fantasy setting supports this approach through ancient structures, supernatural mechanisms, and unusual landscapes. However, exploration lacks the complexity and freedom associated with more expansive RPGs. Some environments feel more like structured pathways than genuinely open locations, limiting opportunities for meaningful discovery. Even so, the combination of puzzles and combat creates a reasonably varied gameplay experience.

Visually, Ethereal Legends benefits from Unreal Engine 4, which helps establish its atmospheric environments and dramatic fantasy scenery. Magical landscapes, imposing architecture, and elaborate lighting contribute to the sense of adventure. The artistic direction demonstrates creativity, particularly considering the project's independent development. However, visual quality remains inconsistent, with character animations and environmental details occasionally revealing technical limitations. The soundtrack complements the setting through fantasy-inspired compositions that enhance exploration and combat. Although the audiovisual presentation is not exceptional, it successfully communicates the intended atmosphere of a mystical world threatened by darkness.

One noteworthy characteristic is the game's open-source development approach, allowing interested developers to examine its underlying programming and potentially experiment with its systems. This decision distinguishes the project from many commercial RPGs and highlights its independent identity. Additional Steam features, including achievements and screenshot functionality, provide supplementary value. Nevertheless, these elements cannot completely overcome the limitations of the core experience. The relatively modest gameplay depth, straightforward progression, and uneven mechanical execution restrict its long-term appeal. Players seeking extensive customization, elaborate character development, or substantial replayability may find the available content insufficient.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Ethereal Legends does not have a confirmed official Verified or Playable classification, making its status Unknown or Unverified. Although controller support may help with handheld operation, it does not guarantee compatibility with SteamOS or Proton. Performance, stability, and control functionality should therefore be considered uncertain without practical testing. Players intending to experience the adventure primarily on Steam Deck should exercise caution.

Ultimately, Ethereal Legends is a creative but uneven fantasy adventure that demonstrates the ambition and limitations of independent development. Its magical combat, atmospheric environments, environmental puzzles, and challenging enemies provide an appealing foundation, but the experience struggles with limited narrative depth and inconsistent gameplay refinement. The game is most suitable for patient RPG enthusiasts willing to overlook technical imperfections while exploring an unconventional independent project. Those expecting sophisticated mechanics and extensive content may find it difficult to recommend. Despite its shortcomings, the dedication behind its creation remains commendable, and several ideas demonstrate genuine potential. 

Rating: 5/10
